criterion.summary: BBH: p_astro > 0.5 (50%) from the targeted BBH analysis, stated as the GWTC-1 standard detection criterion; plus GW170817 (BNS) detected in the full search at FAR < 1 per 100 yr (no p_astro for BNS). The note 'p_astro > 0.5' is correct for the BBHs.
criterion.quote: Our analysis identifies 14 BBH candidates with $\pastro > 50\%$, meeting the standard detection criteria introduced in~\cite{LIGOScientific:2018mvr} and similarly followed in~\cite{Venumadhav:2019lyq}.

supporting_quotes.quote: We identify a population of 14 binary black hole merger events with probability of astrophysical origin $> 0.5$ as well as the binary neutron star merger GW170817.

There are 8 BBH and 1 BNS candidates at a FAR less than 1 per 100 years. These sources are confidently detected in the full analysis without optimizing the search for any specific population of sources.

Several marginal events reported in~\cite{Venumadhav:2019lyq,Venumadhav:2019tad} are found as top candidates, but do not meet our detection threshold based on estimated probability of astrophysical origin.
Our analysis identified GW170817 as a highly significant merger, however, no further individually significant BNS nor NSBH mergers were identified.

tiers.name: confident in full search: FAR < 1 per 100 yr (8 BBH + GW170817)
tiers.quote: There are 8 BBH and 1 BNS candidates at a FAR less than 1 per 100 years. These sources are confidently detected in the full analysis without optimizing the search for any specific population of sources.

tiers.name: targeted BBH, p_astro > 0.5 (further 6)
tiers.quote: When we apply a ranking to search candidates that optimizes search sensitivity for a population of BBH mergers similar to that already detected, we identify a further 6 such mergers with a probability of astrophysical origin above $50\%$. These include GW170818 and GW170729 which were reported in~\cite{LIGOScientific:2018mvr} along with GW170121, GW170727, and GW170304 which were reported in~\cite{Venumadhav:2019lyq}. We report one new marginal BBH candidate, GW151205.

tiers.name: marginal detection (GW151205)
tiers.quote: We confirm the observation of GW170121, GW170304, and GW170727 reported in~\cite{Venumadhav:2019tad} as significant. We also report the marginal detection of GW151205.

below_criterion.count_note: Distinct date designations across Table 2 (30 rows, 17 below), Table 3 (30 rows, 16 below: 14 with p_astro<0.5 plus 2 with p_astro '-'), Table 4 (10 rows, 9 below), deduplicated by exact designation string. None receives a GW-style name; several are discussed by date designation (151216+09:24:16UTC p_astro~0.2 'first identified in 1-OGC'; 151217+03:47:49UTC, 170201+11:03:12UTC, 170629+04:13:55UTC as a possible high-chi_eff population; 170403+23:06:11UTC; 170818+09:34:45UTC judged 'not astrophysical in origin').

open_questions: GW170817 has no p_astro; its inclusion rests on the full-search FAR (<1/10000 yr) and the abstract's 'as well as' wording, not on the p_astro>0.5 rule.

Tier split: Intro says 8 BBH at FAR<1/100 yr in full search + 'a further 6' via p_astro; by Table 2 the 8 are 150914, 170104, 170823, 170814, 151226, 170809, 170608, 151012; the further 6 are 170729, 170121, 170727, 170818, 170304, 151205. GW170304 does not appear in Table 2 (top 30 full search).
GWTC-1 events are referred to only by date designations (e.g. 150914+09:50:45UTC); the paper never writes GW150914, GW151226, GW151012/LVT151012, GW170104, GW170809, GW170814, GW170823.
170814+10:30:43UTC GPS differs by 0.01 s between Tables 2 and 3.
GW151205 (p_astro 0.53) is called both a 'marginal detection' and counted among the 14 BBH with p_astro > 0.5.
